drink-nuoc-ep-chanh-day.atAGlance: Nước ép chanh dây is passion fruit juice, vivid, aromatic, seedy, and sweet-tart over ice.
drink-nuoc-ep-chanh-day.whatItIs: Nước ép chanh dây is passion fruit juice, sharper and more perfumed than many familiar juices.
drink-nuoc-ep-chanh-day.howToEnjoy: Stir before drinking and expect seeds or pulp unless strained.
drink-nuoc-ep-chanh-day.worthKnowing: Passion fruit is common in Vietnamese cafés because it makes drinks taste bright without needing dairy.

drink-rau-ma.atAGlance: Rau má is pennywort juice, green, grassy, and cooling. It is more herbal than fruity.
drink-rau-ma.whatItIs: Rau má is a fresh green drink made from pennywort leaves.
drink-rau-ma.howToEnjoy: Drink it cold and ask less sugar if you want the herbal flavor clear.
drink-rau-ma.worthKnowing: Rau má is part of Vietnam’s cooling-drink culture, often treated as refreshing and restorative.

drink-nuoc-sam.atAGlance: Nước sâm is a sweet herbal drink, usually dark, cooling, and made from a mix of roots, leaves, or dried ingredients.
drink-nuoc-sam.whatItIs: Nước sâm is Vietnamese herbal drink, not ginseng soda in the American sense.
drink-nuoc-sam.howToEnjoy: Drink cold and expect an herbal sweetness. Ask less sweet if it is mixed to order.
drink-nuoc-sam.worthKnowing: Nước sâm belongs to the same cooling-drink world as winter melon tea and pennywort.

drink-nuoc-nha-dam.atAGlance: Nước nha đam is aloe vera drink, usually sweet, cold, and full of soft aloe cubes.
drink-nuoc-nha-dam.whatItIs: Nước nha đam is an aloe drink where the texture of aloe pieces is part of the appeal.
drink-nuoc-nha-dam.howToEnjoy: Drink cold and expect chew. If texture in drinks bothers you, choose juice instead.
drink-nuoc-nha-dam.worthKnowing: Vietnamese drinks often include edible textures, from aloe cubes to basil seeds and jellies.

drink-sam-bo-luong.atAGlance: Sâm bổ lượng is a sweet herbal dessert drink with dried longan, seaweed, lotus seed, jujube, or other cooling ingredients depending on the shop.
drink-sam-bo-luong.whatItIs: Sâm bổ lượng sits between drink and dessert, with spoonable herbal ingredients in sweet syrup.
drink-sam-bo-luong.howToEnjoy: Use a spoon and straw if pieces are included. The textures are part of the drink.
drink-sam-bo-luong.worthKnowing: This is not a simple juice; it reflects a cooling tonic-dessert tradition.

drink-nuoc-la-han-qua.atAGlance: Nước la hán quả is monk fruit herbal drink, usually dark, lightly sweet, and cooling.
drink-nuoc-la-han-qua.whatItIs: Nước la hán quả is a monk fruit drink, often served as a cooling herbal refreshment.
drink-nuoc-la-han-qua.howToEnjoy: Drink cold and ask less sweet if it is brewed with extra sugar.
drink-nuoc-la-han-qua.worthKnowing: La hán quả is prized for natural sweetness, so the drink can feel sweet even before added sugar.

drink-nuoc-suoi.atAGlance: Nước suối is bottled water, the safest simple ask when you want sealed drinking water.
drink-nuoc-suoi.goodToKnow: Ask lạnh if you want it cold, or không đá if you do not want ice.
drink-nuoc-suoi.whatItIs: Nước suối means bottled drinking water in everyday ordering.
drink-nuoc-suoi.howToEnjoy: Ask for a sealed bottle if that matters. Ice may be offered separately.
drink-nuoc-suoi.worthKnowing: For travelers, nước suối is often the easiest water word to use at cafés, shops, and stalls.

drink-nuoc-loc.atAGlance: Nước lọc is plain drinking water. In restaurants it may mean filtered water rather than a sealed bottle.
drink-nuoc-loc.goodToKnow: Ask for nước suối if you specifically want bottled water.
drink-nuoc-loc.whatItIs: Nước lọc means plain filtered water.
drink-nuoc-loc.howToEnjoy: Use it when you want table water. Ask bottled if you need sealed water.
drink-nuoc-loc.worthKnowing: The distinction between nước lọc and nước suối is useful for American travelers.

drink-nuoc-khoang.atAGlance: Nước khoáng is mineral water, usually bottled and sometimes still or sparkling depending on the label.
drink-nuoc-khoang.goodToKnow: Ask có ga for sparkling or không ga for still if the menu is unclear.
drink-nuoc-khoang.howToEnjoy: Order cold or no ice depending on what you trust and prefer.
drink-nuoc-khoang.worthKnowing: Khoáng tells you it is mineral water, while có ga tells you whether it has bubbles.

drink-nuoc-khoang-khong-ga.atAGlance: Nước khoáng không ga is still mineral water: bottled mineral water without carbonation.
drink-nuoc-khoang-khong-ga.goodToKnow: Không ga means not carbonated. It is the still-water counterpart to có ga.
drink-nuoc-khoang-khong-ga.whatItIs: Nước khoáng không ga is still bottled mineral water.
drink-nuoc-khoang-khong-ga.howToEnjoy: Ask for it cold or sealed if that matters.
drink-nuoc-khoang-khong-ga.worthKnowing: Không ga is a useful phrase anywhere sparkling water might be offered.

drink-soda-chanh.atAGlance: Soda chanh is lime soda, fizzy, sweet-sour, and usually served over ice.
drink-soda-chanh.goodToKnow: It can be sweeter than sparkling water. Ask less sugar if you want sharper lime.
drink-soda-chanh.whatItIs: Soda chanh is a made-to-order lime soda, not just a canned soft drink.
drink-soda-chanh.howToEnjoy: Stir before drinking so syrup and lime do not sit at the bottom.
drink-soda-chanh.worthKnowing: Soda chanh is a familiar bridge drink: Vietnamese limeade with bubbles.

drink-soda-chanh-day.atAGlance: Soda chanh dây is passion fruit soda, fizzy, tropical, and sweet-tart.
drink-soda-chanh-day.goodToKnow: Expect pulp or seeds unless the café strains it.
drink-soda-chanh-day.whatItIs: Soda chanh dây is passion fruit mixed with soda water and syrup.
drink-soda-chanh-day.howToEnjoy: Stir well and ask less sweet if you want the passion fruit tartness.
drink-soda-chanh-day.worthKnowing: Passion fruit is a common Vietnamese café flavor because it stays bright in iced drinks.

drink-soda-bac-ha.atAGlance: Soda bạc hà is mint soda, usually green, sweet, fizzy, and cooling.
drink-soda-bac-ha.goodToKnow: Bạc hà means mint. This is syrupy and refreshing, not herbal tea.
drink-soda-bac-ha.whatItIs: Soda bạc hà is mint-flavored soda made with syrup and soda water.
drink-soda-bac-ha.howToEnjoy: Stir before drinking. Ask less syrup if you want it less sweet.
drink-soda-bac-ha.worthKnowing: Vietnamese café sodas are often mixed drinks, so syrup level matters.

drink-nuoc-ngot.atAGlance: Nước ngọt means soft drink, usually a canned or bottled soda.
drink-nuoc-ngot.goodToKnow: Ask what kind if the server offers nước ngọt without naming a brand.
drink-nuoc-ngot.whatItIs: Nước ngọt is the general Vietnamese term for soda or soft drink.
drink-nuoc-ngot.howToEnjoy: Ask cold or no ice if you care how it is served.
drink-nuoc-ngot.worthKnowing: Ngọt means sweet, which helps explain why this phrase covers sodas.

drink-nuoc-tang-luc.atAGlance: Nước tăng lực is energy drink, usually a chilled can or bottle.
drink-nuoc-tang-luc.goodToKnow: Tăng lực means energy. Ask what brand if the menu does not say.
drink-nuoc-tang-luc.whatItIs: Nước tăng lực is the Vietnamese order for an energy drink.
drink-nuoc-tang-luc.howToEnjoy: Order cold and expect a sweet canned drink rather than fresh juice.
drink-nuoc-tang-luc.worthKnowing: Convenience stores and cafés often stock energy drinks beside soda and bottled water.

drink-sua-tuoi.atAGlance: Sữa tươi is fresh milk, usually served cold or used in café drinks.
drink-sua-tuoi.goodToKnow: Ask whether it is sweetened if you want plain milk.
drink-sua-tuoi.howToEnjoy: Drink cold or use the phrase when a coffee shop offers fresh-milk versions.
drink-sua-tuoi.worthKnowing: Fresh milk is different from condensed milk, which is much sweeter and common in Vietnamese coffee.

drink-sua-chua-uong.atAGlance: Sữa chua uống is drinking yogurt, tangy, sweet, and usually bottled or served cold.
drink-sua-chua-uong.goodToKnow: It is more snack drink than plain milk. Ask cold if buying from a shop.
drink-sua-chua-uong.whatItIs: Sữa chua uống is yogurt drink, a sweet-tart dairy drink.
drink-sua-chua-uong.howToEnjoy: Drink chilled and treat it like a small snack.
drink-sua-chua-uong.worthKnowing: Vietnamese dairy drinks often sit beside juice and soda as quick cooling options.
